result:
The proposed answer of √13 is incorrect. The maximum is about 4.148.

**Reachability.** Lamps 1 to 12 form a path, and toggling r flips r−1, r, r+1 among them (lamp 0 is excluded). The toggle matrix is the 12×12 tridiagonal matrix of ones. Its determinant satisfies D_n = D_{n−1} − D_{n−2} with D_0 = D_1 = 1, which has period 6. So D_12 = 1, which is odd, and the matrix is invertible over GF(2). Every on/off pattern of lamps 1 to 12 is therefore reachable, with lamp 0 always on.

**Maximization.** We need the maximum of |s| over all subsets of the 13th roots of unity that contain lamp 0. The best unconstrained subset is a half-circle arc of consecutive lamps. Take the 7 consecutive lamps −3, …, 3, which contain lamp 0. Their sum has magnitude sin(7π/13)/sin(π/13) = sin(6π/13)/sin(π/13) ≈ 0.9927/0.2393 ≈ 4.148. This arc is allowed, since lamp 0 is on and the other lamps are freely settable. Because it is also the best unconstrained choice, 4.148 is the maximum.

Since 4.148 > √13 ≈ 3.606, the proposed answer is wrong.

VERDICT: REJECT
